Bobby Herrerra.thought: I need to find out who had access to Rick’s office after 9:07, since the murder weapon came from there. Margaret, as director of visitor services, likely has keys. Asking her directly about having access will reveal whether she could have taken the marble paperweight. This question is specific, addresses the key information gap, and may implicate or exonerate her. It is not repetitive and is the most useful move now.

Louis Cagliostro.thought: New evidence confirms the murder weapon was Rick’s marble paperweight, which was in his office. Therefore the killer must have had access to the office after 9:07. All current alibis have addressed the bathroom and the office for Tim, Harold, Bobby, and Louis, but Fiona hasn’t been questioned about the office. A single question to Fiona about whether she entered the office after 9:07 will directly test her opportunity. If she says yes, she gains motive and means; if she says no, she can be ruled out. No other suspect’s alibi has been directly challenged with this new clue, so this is the most valuable move.

Pauline Thompson.thought: The only remaining uncertainty is who had access to the marble paperweight after 9:07 and could have brought it into the bathroom. All suspects have denied entering the office after that time, but no one has been directly asked about the paperweight itself. A direct question to a suspect who has not yet been asked could reveal a lie or confirm their alibi. Louis has not been questioned about bringing the paperweight, so asking him should give a clear test of his involvement.

Harold Chun.thought: The new clue that the murder weapon was Rick’s marble paperweight from his office narrows the suspect list to those who had access to the office after 9:07. Only I and Tim had keys. I have no private fact that clears me, but I can ask Tim whether he brought the paperweight into the bathroom after 9:07. This question would directly test whether Tim had the means to commit the murder and would distinguish between the two key‑holders.

Fiona McAllister.thought: Bobby’s private clue gives him a clear opportunity with Rick after he entered the apartment. To test this, ask Bobby whether he and Rick spoke alone in the hallway after Rick entered the apartment. If Bobby is guilty, he will admit, if innocent, he will deny. This should narrow the suspect list.

Margaret Chun.thought: I should ask a question that directly tests whether someone brought the marble paperweight into the bathroom after Rick left. Tim has never been asked about that, and his answer would distinguish him as either the killer (yes) or innocent (no).
